𝐈𝐍 𝐏𝐇𝐎𝐓𝐎𝐒 ||Upon arrival at the scene, the responding EMS team found the patient standing along the roadside, conscious and alert. A primary assessment was immediately conducted to check for active bleeding, deformities, and other apparent injuries. The assessment revealed lacerations on the patient's chin and upper neck. The EMS personnel then assisted the patient in safely ambulating to the ambulance for further assessment, continuous monitoring, and appropriate medical evaluation.
Immediate first aid was administered by the responding EMS personnel. The identified wounds were carefully cleansed and disinfected using povidone-iodine (Betadine) solution to minimize the risk of infection and prevent further contamination.
The patient was transported via BFP Ambulance to Dr. George T. Hofer Medical Center for further medical evaluation and appropriate medical care.

𝐈𝐍 𝐏𝐇𝐎𝐓𝐎𝐒 || While conducting a house-to-house survey at Purok Anunang, Barangay Dalangin, Titay, Zamboanga Sibugay, Shift B personnel received a report of a medical emergency at Palomoc National High School and proceeded to the location. 
Upon arrival at the scene, the responding EMS team found the patient seated inside the school clinic, conscious and initially alert but experiencing hyperventilation and difficulty breathing. Attending teachers reported that the patient had experienced a previous loss of consciousness and that a paper bag had been placed over the patient's mouth. The EMS team conducted an initial assessment, checked the patient's airway, breathing, and circulation, and monitored vital signs and level of consciousness. The patient was assisted into a comfortable seated position, reassured, and encouraged to breathe slowly while being continuously monitored.
The patient was carefully transferred onto a stretcher and secured for transport to the BFP ambulance. The responding EMS personnel provided the necessary support and continuously monitored the patient’s level of consciousness and overall condition during the transfer.
The patient was promptly transported via BFP ambulance to the Titay Rural Health Unit (RHU) for further medical evaluation and management.
Upon arrival at the Titay RHU, the patient was safely transferred and formally endorsed to the physician on duty, together with the pertinent assessment findings, for further medical evaluation and management.

𝐈𝐍 𝐏𝐇𝐎𝐓𝐎𝐒 || Upon arrival at the scene, the responding EMS team found one (1) male patient seated on a chair, conscious and alert but complaining of an inability to move his lower extremities. The patient also exhibited slightly slurred speech. According to the patient's watcher, the patient had just returned from the farm at approximately 1100H when his companions noticed that he was experiencing difficulty breathing. Due to his condition, his companions assisted him and brought him home for further attention. The patient's airway, breathing, circulation, vital signs, and overall condition were assessed and continuously monitored throughout the intervention.
The EMS team carefully assisted the patient onto the stretcher and safely transferred him to the ambulance for transport. His vital signs and overall condition were continuously monitored during the transfer and transport.
The patient was transported via BFP ambulance to Dr. George T. Hofer Medical Center for further medical evaluation and appropriate treatment.
Upon arrival at Dr. George T. Hofer Medical Center, Barangay Tenan, Ipil, Zamboanga Sibugay, the patient was safely transferred and properly endorsed to the medical staff on duty, together with the patient care report and pertinent assessment findings, for further medical evaluation and treatment.

𝐈𝐍 𝐏𝐇𝐎𝐓𝐎𝐒 || Titay Municipal Fire Station (MFS) Shift A personnel provided immediate medical assistance to a 23-year-old female walk-in patient at the fire station in Barangay Poblacion, Titay, Zamboanga Sibugay, who sustained a lacerated wound on the chin and multiple abrasions on the left hand.

Upon initial assessment, the patient was conscious, with active bleeding from a lacerated wound on the chin and multiple abrasions involving the left carpal and metacarpal regions. No other apparent life-threatening injuries were identified during the primary assessment.

Immediate first aid was rendered by applying direct pressure using sterile gauze to control the bleeding, followed by the application of a mild antiseptic solution to the affected areas to help reduce the risk of infection. The patient's vital signs were assessed, and her condition was continuously monitored until the bleeding was controlled.

Medical transport to the nearest appropriate health facility was offered for further evaluation and treatment. However, the patient declined transport after being advised of the importance of medical evaluation. A Refusal of Transport waiver was explained, signed, and properly secured. The patient subsequently left the fire station in stable condition and was advised to seek immediate medical attention if bleeding recurred or other symptoms developed.

Titay MFS reminds the public that prompt first aid and proper medical evaluation are essential in managing wounds and preventing complications.
